text: Two weeks.
One American TV host.
One very confident presidential aspirant.
And a whole continent watching Kenyans on X like it is a Champions League final.
Welcome back to NEXTSCENE TV.
This is How Africa Reacted, Part Two.
Quick recap for those who missed Part One.
On the third of October, a South African user posted that Kenyans want a Twitter war, and it won't end well for them.
That post did more than five million views.
It did not end well.
For him.
By the sixth of October, the fight had spread to Nigeria too, and Sintax summed up the mood.
Kenyans, after cooking two countries in forty-eight hours.
And the rest of Africa?
Popcorn.
All the way from Senegal, Paa Doudou posted in French that the Kenya versus South Africa beef was so funny, he had been crying with laughter since the day before.
When West Africa is laughing at an East Africa versus Southern Africa fight, you know the content is continental.
But October was not done.
On the ninth of October, Newsmax host Rob Finnerty was talking about immigration in America, and he said some American cities were starting to look more like Nairobi than New York.
Big mistake.
Kenyans pointed out that the segment was not even about Kenyan migrants.
Nairobi was just the punchline.
Within hours, his page and the Newsmax page were flooded with photos of the Nairobi skyline, the Expressway, and the tech hubs.
On the thirteenth of October, he posted an apology on X.
He said he misspoke and was sorry to anyone he had offended.
That post has more than three million views.
But KOT were not satisfied.
The insult was on TV, so the apology must also be on TV.
And then, he did it.
Finnerty apologised on air.
Afrocentric shared the clip with a simple message in Swahili.
Apology accepted, don't try to repeat this mistake again.
Here is where it gets interesting.
In the same segment, Finnerty also brought Uganda into it.
But the apology?
Only to Kenya.
And then a post on X went around with the title, What Ugandans can learn from Kenyans.
Unity, patriotism, and defending your country's name.
When your neighbours are writing study notes about you, you have won something.
Then came the plot twist nobody saw coming.
On the thirtieth of September, President Ruto and Aliko Dangote broke ground on a planned sixteen billion dollar refinery in Lamu, targeted for twenty thirty.
Then on the eleventh of October, a video went viral.
Patrick Osoi, who says he is running for president in twenty twenty-seven, told Dangote not to rush the refinery, because once he is sworn in, Dangote will be heading back to Nigeria.
Instablog9ja shared it, and the whole of Nigeria saw it.
Even the Guardian Nigeria covered it, describing Osoi as a former KDF soldier.
Now remember, this is a campaign promise from an aspirant.
It is not government policy, and the refinery has not been cancelled.
Everybody expected Nigerians to defend their billionaire.
Instead?
Look at this.
Pretty replied in pidgin.
If you want to chase him, go ahead and chase him.
Even us citizens never benefited from him, so we won't be too upset.
Daniel said Dangote should fight his own battles, because the refinery meant nothing to ordinary Nigerians.
And Terry gave the best political analysis on the whole internet.
Now Dangote has no option but to fund the campaign of Osoi's opponent.
Politics, explained in one sentence.
So, who won October?
Pablo already has the scoreboard.
Uganda, not even a match.
Tanzania, tukahurumia.
Nigeria, down.
South Africa, down.
Rob Finnerty, apologised.
Who is next?
But honestly, the real winner is Africa.
Kenyans and South Africans roasting each other.
Nigerians agreeing with a Kenyan about their own billionaire.
Senegal laughing.
Uganda taking notes.
The continent has not been this united on the internet in a long time.
So, which country will KOT fight next?
Drop it in the comments.
If you missed Part One, it is linked on screen.
And subscribe to NEXTSCENE TV.
This is just the beginning.
